text:
Marco Rossi came to Vancouver in the Quinn Hughes trade last December, and Saturday he finally played the game that trade was supposed to produce, against the team that sent him. With Elias Pettersson out, Rossi played 19:30, won 12 of 16 faceoffs and scored twice, once on the power play and then the tying goal with the extra attacker and 1:23 left. Vancouver won in a shootout. Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis called it "a beastly game."

The rest of his season has been thinner: 9 points in 23 games and 15:28 a night, with his minutes down about a minute over the last ten while the Canucks lost seven of them. His point rate, 1.54 per 60, sits below our whole range for him (1.71 to 2.52), so the scoring has been the unlucky part, not the role.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.6 wins last season, mostly on the power play, while playing with some of the weakest teammates in the league. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking likes his breakouts: 70% leave the zone with possession. Our projection runs 30 to 49 points.
